name: Humpback Whale
description: Humpback whales sing long, evolving songs that can travel for miles. They team up to “bubble-net” feed, herding fish into a gulp with giant pleated throats.

description.text: Humpback whales sing long, evolving songs that can travel for miles. They team up to “bubble-net” feed, herding fish into a gulp with giant pleated throats.

name: Oceanic Manta Ray
description: Manta rays glide on giant wings, funneling plankton with their head fins. They also visit cleaning stations where small fish remove parasites.

description.text: Manta rays glide on giant “wings,” funneling plankton with unfurling head fins. They loop in graceful barrel rolls over cleaning stations.

name: Ocean Sunfish
description: Among the heaviest bony fish, ocean sunfish feed on jellyfish and other prey. They visit cleaning stations where fish pick off parasites.

description.text: The world’s heaviest bony fish, it drifts like a giant, sideways plate. Feeds on jellyfish and visits cleaning stations where fish pick off parasites.

name: Whale Shark
description: Whale sharks are gentle giants—the largest fish on Earth—filtering plankton and tiny fish with a wide, sieve-like mouth.

description.text: Whale sharks are gentle giants—the largest fish on Earth—filtering plankton and tiny fish with a wide, sieve-like mouth.

name: Blue Whale
description: The blue whale is the largest animal ever known to live on Earth, a massive yet graceful marine mammal that glides through the open ocean.

description.text: The blue whale is the largest animal ever known to live on Earth, a massive yet graceful marine mammal that glides through the open ocean.

name: Basking Shark
description: Despite their colossal size, these gentle giants consume tiny zooplankton by simply swimming with their cavernous mouths wide open.

description.text: Despite their colossal size, these gentle giants consume tiny zooplankton by simply swimming with their cavernous mouths wide open.

name: Megamouth Shark
description: This rare shark filters tiny prey, including krill, through its enormous mouth. Its pale upper lip reflects light; it does not produce its own glow.

description.text: A deep-sea, filter-feeding fish that features a unique glowing band on its upper jaw to attract prey in the dark.

name: Reef Manta Ray
description: Reef manta rays filter plankton with their head fins and visit cleaning stations. Unique patterns of belly spots help researchers identify individuals.

description.text: The reef manta ray boasts the largest brain-to-body mass ratio of any cold-blooded fish species. They can launch themselves up to 10 feet out of the water.

name: Hammerhead
description: They use their wide heads to sweep the ocean floor like a metal detector. They use thousands of tiny electrical sensors to find buried creatures.

description.text: They use their wide heads to sweep the ocean floor like a metal detector. They use thousands of tiny electrical sensors to find buried creatures.

name: Great White
description: An apex hunter that shapes the whole food web. Built for ambush: countershaded body hides it in sunlit seas.

description.text: An apex hunter that shapes the whole food web. Built for ambush: countershaded body hides it in sunlit seas.

name: Bull Shark
description: Bull sharks can live in both salt and freshwater, cruising far up rivers—even hundreds of miles inland.

description.text: Bull sharks can live in both salt and freshwater, cruising far up rivers—even hundreds of miles inland.

name: Tiger Shark
description: A large, powerful predator found in warm ocean waters around the world, it has a broad diet and a reputation as an opportunistic hunter.

description.text: A large, powerful predator found in warm ocean waters around the world, it has a broad diet and a reputation as an opportunistic hunter.

name: Killer Whale
description: Orcas are the largest members of the dolphin family. Their close-knit groups use different hunting traditions to catch fish, seals, or other whales.

description.text: The ultimate apex predator of the ocean, Orcas are known as “Killer Whales” for their ability to take down the largest and most feared ocean creatures.

name: Pilot Whale
description: Pilot whales live in close-knit pods led by experienced females. Deep divers, they chase squid in the dark and keep tight social bonds.

description.text: Pilot whales live in close-knit pods led by experienced females. Deep divers, they chase squid in the dark and keep tight social bonds.

name: Bottlenose Dolphin
description: Bottlenose dolphins are intelligent, social marine mammals with sleek gray bodies and short snouts. They use echolocation to find prey.

description.text: Bottlenose dolphins are highly intelligent and social marine mammals recognized by their sleek grey bodies, short snouts, and playful, acrobatics.

name: Giant Squid
description: With enormous eyes adapted to dim light, giant squid roam the ocean depths. Two long feeding tentacles reach out to snatch fish and other squid.

description.text: Possessing the largest eyes in the animal kingdom, it roams the lightless ocean depths using two long feeding tentacles to snatch prey.

name: Colossal Squid
description: The heaviest known squid lives in the cold Southern Ocean. Rotating hooks on its tentacle clubs help it hold slippery prey.

description.text: The largest, and most elusive invertebrate on the planet, no human has ever witnessed an adult colossal squid alive.

name: Greenland Shark
description: A slow-moving deep-water apex predator famous for having the longest known lifespan of all vertebrate animals.

description.text: A slow-moving deep-water apex predator famous for having the longest known lifespan of all vertebrate animals.

name: Giant Phantom Jelly
description: Unlike most jellyfish, the giant phantom jelly lacks stinging tentacles. Instead, it uses its long arms to trap plankton and small fish.

description.text: Unlike most jellyfish, the giant phantom jelly lacks stinging tentacles. Instead, it uses its long arms to trap plankton and small fish.

name: Sperm Whale
description: The largest toothed predators on Earth, sperm whales hunt for giant squid in the ocean deep using incredibly loud echolocation clicks.

description.text: The largest toothed predators on Earth, sperm whales hunt for giant squid in the ocean deep using incredibly loud echolocation clicks.

name: Shortfin Mako Shark
description: A powerful, fast-swimming shark, the shortfin mako pursues fish and squid. It can retain heat in parts of its body to stay active in cool water.

description.text: The ocean's fastest fish capable of swimming bursts over 46 mph. It has specialized scales along its flanks to greatly reduce hydrodynamic drag.

name: Black Marlin
description: Black marlin hunt fish and squid with a long, spear-like bill. Their rigid pectoral fins cannot fold flat against the sides of the body.

description.text: A massive, highly sought-after predatory saltwater game fish that is said to reach speeds of up to 65 mph for short bursts.

name: Swordfish
description: Charging through the pitch-black twilight zone, the swordfish uses its razor-sharp bill to slash and stun fast-moving schools of squid and fish.

description.text: Charging through the pitch-black twilight zone, the swordfish uses its razor-sharp bill to slash and stun fast-moving schools of squid and fish.

name: Bluefin Tuna
description: Atlantic bluefin tuna retain heat in their muscles and other tissues. This helps them pursue prey across both cool and warm ocean waters.

description.text: These colossal fish are warm-blooded, allowing them to regulate their body temperature and travel from freezing arctic to warm tropical waters.

name: Great Barracuda
description: Barracudas hover like steel spears, then explode forward in a silver blur to snatch prey with dagger teeth. They are drawn to flashes of light.

description.text: Barracudas hover like steel spears, then explode forward in a silver blur to snatch prey with dagger teeth. They are drawn to flashes of light.

name: Green Moray Eel
description: Moray eels lurk in crevices. They snatch prey, then fire out a second set of jaws (pharyngeal jaws) to pull it down.

description.text: Moray eels lurk in crevices. They snatch prey, then fire out a second set of jaws (pharyngeal jaws) to pull it down.

name: Reef Shark
description: Blacktip reef sharks are shallow-reef sprinters with signature black-tipped fins. They dart through lagoons at dawn and dusk, snapping up small fish.

description.text: Blacktip reef sharks are shallow-reef sprinters with signature black-tipped fins. They dart through lagoons at dawn and dusk, snapping up small fish.

name: Goliath Grouper
description: Groupers are ambush hunters that gulp prey with a sudden vacuum from their huge mouths. They lurk in shadows, waiting for prey.

description.text: Groupers are ambush hunters that gulp prey with a sudden vacuum from their huge mouths. They lurk in shadows, waiting for prey.

name: Green Sea Turtle
description: Adult green turtles graze mainly on seagrass and algae. After long ocean migrations, females return to their natal nesting regions to lay eggs.

description.text: Green sea turtles graze on seagrass and algae. After long ocean migrations, females return to the very beaches where they hatched to nest.

name: Spinner Dolphins
description: Spinner dolphins leap in tight, corkscrew spins that can launch them high above the waves. They can spin up to 7 times in the air.

description.text: Spinner dolphins leap in tight, corkscrew spins that can launch them high above the waves. They can spin up to 7 times in the air.

name: Thresher Shark
description: A thresher shark is a sleek, fast-swimming ocean predator famous for its extraordinarily long, whip-like tail that it uses to stun prey.

description.text: A thresher shark is a sleek, fast-swimming ocean predator famous for its extraordinarily long, whip-like tail that it uses to stun prey.

name: Goblin Shark
description: The goblin shark is a rare, deep-sea species recognized by its long snout and slingshot-like jaws that extend to capture prey

description.text: The goblin shark is a rare, deep-sea species recognized by its long snout and slingshot-like jaws that extend to capture prey

name: Gulper Eel
description: The gulper eel's enormous mouth and expandable throat can engulf prey. A tiny light-producing organ sits at the tip of its long, whip-like tail.

description.text: A bizarre deep-sea fish characterized by its massive, unhinged pelican-like jaw and a long, whip-like tail.

name: Deep Sea Skate
description: Found in extreme depths of up to 3km, these resilient marine creatures gracefully glide over the ocean floor to hunt for bottom dwellers.

description.text: Found in extreme depths of up to 3km, these resilient marine creatures gracefully glide over the ocean floor to hunt for bottom dwellers.

name: Chimera
description: Often referred to as a "ghost shark," this bizarre creature is famous for its shimmering, scaleless skin, large rabbit-like eyes.

description.text: Often referred to as a "ghost shark," this bizarre creature is famous for its shimmering, scaleless skin, large rabbit-like eyes.

name: Frilled Shark
description: Six pairs of frilly gill slits give this deep-water shark its name. Its eel-like body and rows of three-pointed teeth help it capture prey.

description.text: This sea-serpent like predator strikes its prey with a quick, snake-like lunge and holds them fast with an arsenal of over 300 needle-sharp teeth.

name: Cookie Cutter
description: Cookiecutter sharks use thick lips to grip larger animals and sharp lower teeth to cut round plugs of flesh. Their undersides glow with bioluminescence.

description.text: It uses bioluminescence on its underside to disguise itself as a harmless fish, tricking large predators into approaching so it can bite them.

name: Silky Shark
description: A swift, pelagic shark that gets its name from its exceptionally smooth, soft skin, which is covered in densely packed overlapping scales.

description.text: A swift, pelagic shark that gets its name from its exceptionally smooth, soft skin, which is covered in densely packed overlapping scales.

name: Oceanic Whitetip Shark
description: Long, rounded pectoral fins and white-tipped fins distinguish this open-ocean shark. It searches warm seas for fish, squid, and other food.

description.text: Their senses are highly tuned, they can recognize the specific sound of slowing boat engines as a sign of an easy meal.

name: Blue Shark
description: Blue sharks make long migrations through temperate and tropical seas. Their slender bodies and long pectoral fins suit life in the open ocean.

description.text: The most heavily fished shark in the world and can travel over 5,000 miles during their massive oceanic migrations.

name: Galápagos Shark
description: Galapagos sharks favor clear, warm water around oceanic islands. These large requiem sharks patrol reef edges and feed mainly on fish.

description.text: A bold, highly inquisitive requiem shark that is known for circling divers and boats. It aggressively patrols the open waters around islands worldwide.

name: Yellowfin Tuna
description: They utilize a biological hydraulic system that pumps fluid into their fins, instantly stiffening them to execute razor-sharp, high-speed turns.

description.text: They utilize a biological hydraulic system that pumps fluid into their fins, instantly stiffening them to execute razor-sharp, high-speed turns.

name: Sailfish
description: Sailfish use their long bills to slash or tap schooling prey. They raise their large dorsal fins while hunting and fold them down when swimming quickly.

description.text: Widely considered the fastest fish in the sea, capable of burst swimming speeds of up to 70 miles per hour.

name: Wahoo
description: Wahoo are streamlined predators with sharp teeth and blue bars along their sides. They hunt fish and squid in warm ocean waters.

description.text: The wahoo is a sleek, razor-toothed marine predator capable of swimming at blistering speeds up to 48 miles per hour to ambush prey.

name: Loggerhead
description: Loggerheads use large heads and powerful jaws to crush crabs, whelks, and other hard-shelled prey. Adults travel widely between feeding and nesting areas.

description.text: The largest hard-shelled sea turtle alive, it crushes hard-shelled prey like crabs, whelks, and horseshoe crabs.

name: Nurse Shark
description: Nurse sharks can rest completely still on the ocean floor and pump water directly over their gills to breathe, unlike many other shark species.

description.text: Nurse sharks can rest completely still on the ocean floor and pump water directly over their gills to breathe, unlike many other shark species.

name: Yellow-Lipped Sea Krait
description: Yellow-lipped sea kraits hunt eels underwater with potent venom. Unlike fully aquatic sea snakes, they come ashore to rest, digest meals, and lay eggs.

description.text: It possesses a powerful neurotoxic venom (alpha-neurotoxins) that attacks the nervous system, causing paralysis and respiratory failure.

name: Emerald Crab
description: Emerald crabs prowl at night, picking algae and leftovers with spoon-tipped claws. Their leafy green shell hides them among corals.

description.text: Emerald crabs prowl at night, picking algae and leftovers with spoon-tipped claws. Their leafy green shell hides them among corals.

name: Sea Urchin
description: Long-spined sea urchins graze on algae and help keep reef surfaces clear. Their slender spines defend them while tube feet grip and move over rocks.

description.text: Despite being lacking a brain, heart, or lungs, it possesses hundreds of tiny, glowing blue dots on its shell that act as sensitive light receptors.

name: Anemone
description: Sea anemones anchor to rock and hunt with stinging tentacles packed with tiny harpoons. Some host clownfish, trading shelter for scraps.

description.text: Sea anemones anchor to rock and hunt with stinging tentacles packed with tiny harpoons. Some host clownfish, trading shelter for scraps.

name: Blue Crab
description: Blue crabs swim with paddle-shaped rear legs. They shed their shells to grow, leaving them briefly soft until the new shell hardens.

description.text: Blue crabs are fast swimmers with paddle-shaped back legs and bright blue claws. They molt to grow—briefly becoming soft-shells

name: Arrow Crab
description: Arrow crabs tiptoe on stilt-like legs, their long “arrow” snout probing crevices. At night they scavenge around for leftovers.

description.text: Arrow crabs tiptoe on stilt-like legs, their long “arrow” snout probing crevices. At night they scavenge around for leftovers.

name: Mantis Shrimp
description: Mantis shrimp hunt with specialized clubs or spears. Club-bearing species strike so fast that collapsing cavitation bubbles add a second impact.

description.text: Mantis shrimp strike with club or spear arms so fast they create cavitation bubbles—tiny shockwave “explosions” that stun prey.

name: Leather Starfish
description: Leather stars have smooth, rubbery skin and a garlic-like odor. Tube feet carry them over rocky Pacific shores as they feed on anemones and other prey.

description.text: Leather starfish wear smooth, rubbery skin instead of spines, often mottled orange, brown, or purple. They glide on hundreds of tube feet to graze anemones

name: Cleaner Shrimp
description: Scarlet cleaner shrimp wave long white antennae at cleaning stations. Fish visit to have parasites and dead tissue removed from their skin and mouths.

description.text: Cleaner shrimp set up “stations,” waving long white antennae to invite fish clients. They pluck parasites and dead skin  earning protection for their service.

name: Crown of Thorns
description: Crown-of-thorns sea stars spread their stomachs over corals to digest living tissue outside their bodies. Venomous spines help deter predators.

description.text: They crawl over corals using their arms to blanket a colony and rasp away living tissue. Their long venomous spines deter predators.

name: Nudibranch
description: The magnificent chromodoris is a brightly patterned, sponge-eating sea slug. Chemicals obtained from its food help defend it against predators.

description.text: Their bright patterns warn of potent chemical defenses. Some steal stinging cells from their prey and reuse them as toxic armor.

name: Giant Triton
description: Giant tritons are large predatory sea snails that hunt crown-of-thorns starfish, subduing them with a paralyzing bite.

description.text: Giant tritons are large predatory sea snails that hunt crown-of-thorns starfish, subduing them with a paralyzing bite.

name: Octopus
description: Octopuses change color and texture in a blink, melting into reef or rock. With eight clever arms and hundreds of suckers, they solve puzzles—then vanish in a puff of ink.

description.text: Octopuses change color and texture in a blink, melting into reef or rock. With eight clever arms and hundreds of suckers, they solve puzzles—then vanish in a puff of ink.

name: Oysters
description: Oysters are a vital component of marine ecosystems, primarily functioning as filter feeders that significantly improve water quality and create complex reef habitats.

description.text: Oysters are a vital component of marine ecosystems, primarily functioning as filter feeders that significantly improve water quality and create complex reef habitats.

name: Giant Clam
description: Giant clams are the largest living bivalves. Living in warm, shallow coral reefs, they anchor themselves and rely on symbiotic algae for much of their energy.

description.text: Giant clams are the largest living bivalves. Living in warm, shallow coral reefs, they anchor themselves and rely on symbiotic algae for much of their energy.

name: Deep Cucumber
description: Deep-sea sea cucumbers feed on organic particles on or near the seafloor. Their soft bodies and feeding tentacles come in many shapes across species.

description.text: Deep-sea cucumbers look remarkably soft, blobby, and fleshy—often resembling a cross between a worm and a gelatinous slug.

name: Brittlestar
description: Brittle stars move with slender, flexible arms joined to a central disc. Many can shed an arm to escape a predator and later regrow it.

description.text: Brittlestars  have five long, snakelike arms that easily snap off and regrow to help them escape predators.

name: Vampire Squid
description: When threatened, it doesn't ink; instead, it cloaks itself by pulling its webbed arms over its head and releases glowing, bioluminescent clouds.

description.text: When threatened, it doesn't ink; instead, it cloaks itself by pulling its webbed arms over its head and releases glowing, bioluminescent clouds.

name: Giant Isopod
description: Giant isopods are deep-sea relatives of woodlice. Their armored bodies protect them as they scavenge, and a slow metabolism helps them endure long fasts.

description.text: Often described as a resilient underwater tank, this living fossil features a tough exoskeleton. It can survive years between feedings.

name: Giant Tube Worm
description: Giant tube worms live at hydrothermal vents. Without a mouth or gut, adults rely on internal bacteria that use chemicals from vent fluids to make food.

description.text: Lives in pitch-black, toxic environments relying on symbiotic bacteria for food. It builds a tough, protective tube to bear harsh temperatures.

name: Peacock Squid
description: Peacock squid have large eyes and nearly transparent bodies. Light organs beneath the eyes help hide their silhouettes from predators below.

description.text: It emits faint bioluminescent light from photophores located just beneath its eyes to help camouflage it’s silhouette.

name: Deep Sea Jelly
description: Atolla jellyfish can flash rings of blue bioluminescence when disturbed. This burglar-alarm display may draw larger predators toward an attacker.

description.text: It possess the unique ability to flash bioluminescent blue when attacked to attract other predators to scare off the attacker.

name: Dumbo Octopus
description: To hunt they hover right above the seafloor and "hoover" up worms, snails, and crustaceans, swallowing their prey whole.

description.text: To hunt they hover right above the seafloor and "hoover" up worms, snails, and crustaceans, swallowing their prey whole.

name: Giant Red Shrimp
description: Famous for its vivid, deep red coloration, extremely long antennae, and a prominent crest.

description.text: Famous for its vivid, deep red coloration, extremely long antennae, and a prominent crest.

name: Portuguese Man O’ War
description: A Portuguese man o' war is a colony of specialized zooids. Its gas-filled float rides at the surface while long, stinging tentacles capture prey below.

description.text: Despite looking like a single animal, the Portuguese man o' war is actually a bizarre colony of thousands of genetically identical, clones called zooids.

name: Blue Sea Dragon
description: Blue sea dragons float upside down at the surface. They eat animals such as the Portuguese man o' war and store stolen stinging cells for defense.

description.text: It survives by eating highly venomous creatures like the Portuguese Man O' War, stealing their stinging cells, to use for it’s own defense.

name: Market Squid
description: Market squid live only about six to nine months. They gather to mate and lay egg capsules on the seafloor, then die after spawning.

description.text: After mating in massive swarms, the entire population dies within a year, leaving their fertilized eggs to hatch the next generation.

name: Box Jellyfish
description: The Australian box jellyfish has a cube-shaped bell and clusters of eyes. Its long tentacles carry powerful venom for catching fish and shrimp.

description.text: Considered the most venomous marine creature on Earth, it carries a potent venom that can kill a human within just two to five minutes of a sting.

name: Lionfish
description: Lionfish spread their broad fins to corner small fish before striking. Their defensive spines are venomous; introduced populations threaten Atlantic reefs.

description.text: Lionfish drift like ornate fans, herding small fish with wide fins before a lightning strike. Their spines are venomous and can overrun reefs.

name: Winter Flounder
description: Flounders lie flat and camouflaged, burying in sand with both eyes on one side. They ambush prey with a sudden snap.

description.text: Flounders lie flat and camouflaged, burying in sand with both eyes on one side. They ambush prey with a sudden snap.

name: Wrasse - Cleaner
description: Cleaner wrasses run reef “stations” where big fish queue for a cleanup. They pick off parasites and dead skin—earning a safe meal and trust.

description.text: Cleaner wrasses run reef “stations” where big fish queue for a cleanup. They pick off parasites and dead skin—earning a safe meal and trust.

name: Parrotfish - Fairy
description: Parrotfish scrape food from reef surfaces with beak-like teeth, helping produce sand. Some species sleep inside protective mucus cocoons.

description.text: They scrape algae with a beak-like bite, grinding coral into fine sand. Some wrap in a nighttime mucus cocoon to hide their scent from predators.

name: Grunt - Bluestriped
description: Bluestriped grunts gather over reefs by day and feed over sand and seagrass at night. They make grunting sounds by rubbing their throat teeth.

description.text: Grunts school roam seagrass beds to feed at night. They “grunt” by rubbing pharyngeal teeth, a sound that echoes through the reef.

name: Clownfish
description: Bearing bright orange and white markings, they are renowned for their unique ability to safely live inside venomous sea anemones without getting stung.

description.text: Bearing bright orange and white markings, they are renowned for their unique ability to safely live inside venomous sea anemones without getting stung.

name: Spanish Hogfish
description: Young Spanish hogfish clean parasites from other fish. Adults feed on bottom-dwelling invertebrates, and some females later change into males.

description.text: Featuring a pig-like snout they use to root out crabs and clams. Most start life as females and later turn male, flashing quick color changes.

name: Triggerfish - Picasso
description: Known for its striking colors and pugnacious attitude, this triggerfish can lock its dorsal spine into coral crevices for protection.

description.text: Known for its striking colors and pugnacious attitude, this triggerfish can lock its dorsal spine into coral crevices for protection.

name: Porcupine Fish
description: Porcupinefish puff into a spiky ball to scare off predators. Their beak crushes shells, and some species carry a powerful toxin.

description.text: Porcupinefish puff into a spiky ball to scare off predators. Their beak crushes shells, and some species carry a powerful toxin.

name: French Angelfish
description: French angelfish cruise reefs in bonded pairs, flashing yellow-edged scales and a dark mask.

description.text: French angelfish cruise reefs in bonded pairs, flashing yellow-edged scales and a dark mask.

name: Sargeant Major
description: Sergeant major damselfish wear bold black-and-white bars with a splash of yellow on top. Males fiercely guard egg patches.

description.text: Sergeant major damselfish wear bold black-and-white bars with a splash of yellow on top. Males fiercely guard egg patches.

name: Longhorn Cowfish
description: Protected by a rigid, box-like body, longhorn cowfish graze on small bottom-dwelling prey. When severely stressed, they can release toxic mucus.

description.text: When severely threatened, the longhorn cowfish secretes a potent neurotoxin creating an invisible cloud that can kill any creatures in close proximity.

name: Spotfin Butterflyfish
description: A black spot near the rear of the dorsal fin gives the spotfin butterflyfish its name. A dark stripe crosses its eye as it forages around reefs.

description.text: The twinspot butterflyfish is recognized by the two distinctive dark spots on each side of its body, to confuse predators.

name: Queen Angelfish
description: The Queen Angelfish is a brilliantly colored reef fish that glides through warm, clear Caribbean shallows, recognizable by its vivid colors.

description.text: The Queen Angelfish is a brilliantly colored reef fish that glides through warm, clear Caribbean shallows, recognizable by its vivid colors.

name: Blue Tang
description: An active herbivore that shifts between territorial, wandering, and schooling social phases. It grazes continuously on algae.

description.text: An active herbivore that shifts between territorial, wandering, and schooling social phases. It grazes continuously on algae.

name: Frogfish
description: Frogfish hide among reef growth and lure prey with a modified dorsal-fin spine. Their expanding mouths suck in unsuspecting animals in a rapid gulp.

description.text: Frogfish vanish in plain sight. They “fish” with a built-in lure, then gulp prey with one of the fastest strikes in the ocean.

name: Parrotfish - Spectacled
description: Known for its distinctive “spectacle-like” markings around the eyes and beak, it contributes to sand production through its feeding.

description.text: Known for its distinctive “spectacle-like” markings around the eyes and beak, it contributes to sand production through its feeding.

name: Bristlemouth
description: Bristlemouths are tiny deep-sea fish considered the most abundant vertebrates on Earth, with populations in the quadrillions.

description.text: Bristlemouths are tiny deep-sea fish considered the most abundant vertebrates on Earth, with populations in the quadrillions.

name: Owlfish
description: These stealthy predators drift through pitch-black environments using their massive eyes to spot the faintest glimmers of bioluminescent prey.

description.text: These stealthy predators drift through pitch-black environments using their massive eyes to spot the faintest glimmers of bioluminescent prey.

name: Pacific Grenadier
description: Often called a "rattail" because of its slender, whip-like tail, this deep-sea fish can live for over 70 years in extreme pressures.

description.text: Often called a "rattail" because of its slender, whip-like tail, this deep-sea fish can live for over 70 years in extreme pressures.

name: Viperfish
description: Long, needle-like teeth help viperfish hold slippery prey. Light-producing organs on their bodies and dorsal-fin lure shine in the deep sea.

description.text: Because its teeth are too long to fit in its mouth, they curve backward and can extend up behind its eyes.

name: Anglerfish - Humpback
description: Female humpback anglerfish carry a lure lit by symbiotic bacteria. It dangles above the mouth, drawing prey close in the darkness of the deep sea.

description.text: The tip of their dorsal fin contains a glowing sac of bioluminescent bacteria used to attract prey in the pitch-black ocean depths.

name: Barrel Eye Fish
description: A transparent dome protects the barreleye's tubular green eyes. The eyes can rotate from looking upward to facing forward as the fish feeds.

description.text: The barreleye boasts a cockpit-like, see-through head that allows its internal organs and green eyes to be visible.

name: Fangtooth Fish
description: Fangtooth fish have enormous teeth for their small bodies. Special sockets in the roof of the mouth make room for the long lower fangs.

description.text: A small but fearsome-looking deep-sea predator renowned for having the largest teeth-to-body ratio of any fish in the ocean.

name: Black Swallower
description: The black swallower has an elastic stomach that can hold prey larger than itself. This adaptation helps it take advantage of scarce deep-sea meals.

description.text: A deep-sea fish known for its highly distensible stomach, allowing it to consume prey over twice its length and 10 times its mass.

name: Tripod Fish
description: Tripod fish stand above the seabed on three elongated fin rays. Facing into the current, they spread their pectoral fins to help detect drifting prey.

description.text: Completely blind, it rests on the ocean floor using three extraordinarily long, stiff fin rays to both elevate its body and move prey to it’s mouth.

name: Coelacanth
description: West Indian Ocean coelacanths have fleshy, lobed fins and a distinctive three-part tail. These deep-water fish belong to an ancient lineage.

description.text: Often dubbed "living fossils", coelacanths are rare, lobe-finned fish that can reach weights nearing 200lbs.

name: Flying Fish
description: It escapes underwater predators by rocketing to the surface and using its rigid, wing-like fins to glide gracefully through the air for hundreds of feet.

description.text: It escapes underwater predators by rocketing to the surface and using its rigid, wing-like fins to glide gracefully through the air for hundreds of feet.

name: Barracuda
description: Barracudas wait near prey before lunging with bursts of speed. Their streamlined bodies and sharp teeth help them catch other fish.

description.text: Often dubbed the "Tiger of the Sea", the Barracuda is a fast, predator that relies on ambush and bursts of speed up to 35 mph to catch prey.

name: Mahi-Mahi (Dolphinfish)
description: Mahi-mahi grow rapidly in warm ocean waters. They hunt fish and squid, often gathering near floating seaweed, logs, and other objects.

description.text: One of the fastest-growing wild fish in the ocean, they can explode from tiny larvae to over 4 feet long and 40 pounds in just their first year of life.

name: King Mackerel
description: A highly sought-after, migratory coastal pelagic fish that is renowned for "skyrocketing" clear out of the water when aggressively attacking prey.

description.text: A highly sought-after, migratory coastal pelagic fish that is renowned for "skyrocketing" clear out of the water when aggressively attacking prey.

name: Tripletail
description: The tripletail is a master of surface deception. It drifts sideways to mimic floating dead leaves and fool its prey.

description.text: The tripletail is a master of surface deception. It drifts sideways to mimic floating dead leaves and fool its prey.

name: Halfbeak
description: Halfbeaks have a long lower jaw and a much shorter upper jaw. These surface-dwelling fish may leap or skip across the water to escape predators.

description.text: Many halfbeak species are capable of breaching the water's surface to "fly" or skip across the waves to escape predators, much like flying fish.

name: Needlefish
description: Needlefish hunt near the surface with long jaws lined with sharp teeth. When startled, they can leap clear of the water.

description.text: Needlefish are hyper-fast, slender ocean hunters known to skip across the water at speeds up to 40 mph, sometimes running into swimmers.

name: Bluefin Tuna (Juvenile)
description: Young Atlantic bluefin tuna grow quickly and gather in schools. They eat small fish, squid, and crustaceans as they develop into powerful ocean hunters.

description.text: They transform in size from nearly microscopic larvae to 3-foot predatory fish in just three years, gathering in large, protective schools.

name: Remora
description: A modified dorsal fin forms the remora's suction disc. It attaches to larger marine animals for transport and feeds on scraps or parasites.

description.text: Thanks to a dorsal fin designed serve as an oval suction disc, remoras can hitch free rides and clean parasites off much larger marine animals like sharks

name: Bluefish
description: Bluefish are the only living species in the family Pomatomidae. Schools of these sharp-toothed predators pursue smaller fish in coastal waters.

description.text: The notoriously aggressive Bluefish is the only living member of its entire scientific family and lacks any known living relatives.

name: Bonito
description: Bonitos are streamlined relatives of tunas and mackerels. They hunt small schooling fish, squid, and crustaceans in open coastal waters.

description.text: Bonito are swift, predatory members of the tuna family that can reach explosive swimming speeds of up to 40 miles per hour

name: Crevalle Jack
description: Crevalle jacks are powerful coastal predators that often hunt in schools. They can make grunting sounds using their teeth and swim bladder.

description.text: When pulled from the water, they produce distinct, loud croaking sounds by grinding their teeth together and resonating its air bladder.

name: Yellowtail Amberjack
description: Yellowtail amberjacks are strong-swimming predators with a yellow tail and side stripe. They school around rocky reefs and hunt fish and squid.

description.text: A prized gamefish and capable swimmer often referred to by anglers as a "reef donkey" because of its incredible fighting power and strength.

name: Frigate Tuna
description: Frigate tuna form large schools in warm seas. They pursue small fish, squid, and crustaceans and may also feed on members of their own species.

description.text: The frigate tuna is a highly social, fast-swimming schooling predator that occasionally practices cannibalism by feeding on it’s own kind.

name: Lookdown
description: The lookdown gets its name from its steep forehead and high-set eyes. Its thin, silvery body reflects light as it swims in coastal schools.

description.text: It gets it’s name from having high-set eyes and steep profile make it look like it is permanently peering down its nose.

name: Pompano
description: Florida pompano forage over sandy bottoms for small crustaceans and mollusks. These silvery fish often travel in schools along the surf zone.

description.text: These fast-swimming schooling fish are actually completely toothless, relying instead on hard bony plates in their throats to crush their prey.

name: Ocean Triggerfish
description: Ocean triggerfish swim above reefs and drop-offs, feeding on plankton and small animals. They can lock their first dorsal spine upright for defense.

description.text: This species spends its life in the open ocean, frequently darting in and out of floating mats of Sargassum seaweed.

name: African Pompano
description: Young African pompano trail long, thread-like fin rays that resemble jellyfish tentacles. These streamers shorten as the fish grow into silvery adults.

description.text: They have tremendously long, thread-like fin tips resembling jellyfish tentacles, which recede as the fish grow into shimmering adults.

name: Krill Bloom
description: Krill are small, shrimp-like crustaceans that gather in dense swarms. These shifting groups provide food for whales, seals, seabirds, and fish.

description.text: A highly concentrated, massive defensive swarm of krill containing up to millions of individual crustaceans.

name: Sardine School
description: Sardines gather in shifting schools that tighten when predators approach. School size and mass vary as fish join, leave, and move together.

description.text: They are famed for traveling in massive, synchronized schools reaching up to 20 meters in diameter.

name: Anchovy Swarm
description: Anchovies are small schooling fish that feed on plankton. Their shifting schools support predators ranging from seabirds to much larger fish.

description.text: A small, silver, open-ocean schooling fish which filter microscopic plankton and sustain entire marine ecosystems.

name: Silverside Flash
description: Atlantic silversides form shimmering schools in shallow coastal water. Their silver stripes reflect light as the group turns together.

description.text: They flash their reflective silver stripes in massive, synchronized schools to blind and disorient attacking predators.

description: White grunts school around reefs by day and forage at night. They make low grunting sounds by rubbing teeth in their throats.

description.text: They produce low,“grunt” sounds especially when disturbed or communicating in groups.

name: Emperor Angelfish
description: When startled, adult emperor angelfishes can produce a loud, audible thumping or knocking sound that resembles a drum roll.
